principles: Keep implementation stories cohesive and independently reversible
Do not trade liveness fixes for weaker evidence or role separation
drivers: Six failures were observed in one lifecycle but belong to five subsystems
The document must be immediately usable for story intake
Several naive fixes can introduce silent authorization or coverage regressions

options.name: A: One umbrella plan with five implementation workstreams
pros: Provides shared dependency and rollout model
Keeps runtime changes in cohesive future stories
cons: Implementation completion will be distributed across later stories

options.name: B: One implementation story for all six failures
cons: Rollback and root-cause attribution become difficult
Session identity design can block faster liveness fixes

options.name: C: Six isolated documents
cons: Makes dependency and sequencing hard to audit

chosen: A: One umbrella plan with five implementation workstreams
rationale: The diagnosis is cross-cutting, but the fixes have different owners and failure domains. An umbrella plan records shared invariants and ordering while future stories remain small, testable, and reversible.

preMortem.scenario: The umbrella plan contradicts an existing canonical decision document
preMortem.trigger: It restates subsystem behavior instead of referencing the owner document
preMortem.consequence: Future implementers follow conflicting truth sources
preMortem.mitigation: Declare precedence and label this document as execution coordination only

preMortem.scenario: A timeout or receipt-reuse fix weakens DONE evidence freshness
preMortem.trigger: Reuse checks omit HEAD, material, story files, policy, or command-set binding
preMortem.consequence: Stale validation is accepted as current
preMortem.mitigation: Make all binding fields explicit acceptance criteria and require negative stale cases

preMortem.scenario: Stable session identity collapses reviewer and implementer identities
preMortem.trigger: A repository-global or thread-only token is shared across roles
preMortem.consequence: Lease and anti-self-review boundaries are bypassed
preMortem.mitigation: Require task identity plus distinct agent/role identity and cross-role collision tests

preMortem.scenario: IDF filtering hides an explicitly relevant decision document
preMortem.trigger: High document frequency filtering applies to paths or relatedDocs
preMortem.consequence: Review coverage regresses while scan cost looks lower
preMortem.mitigation: Exempt explicit paths, relatedDocs, registry facts, and typed risk signals from generic-token filtering
